brief: A 6-second animated bar chart: five bars labelled Mon to Fri grow from zero to heights 3, 7, 5, 9, 4 with value labels, and the tallest bar is highlighted at the end.
checks: The video shows exactly five vertical bars (no more, no less).
The bars are labeled underneath (or above) with the day abbreviations Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri in that left‑to‑right order.
Each bar’s final height matches the specified value: Mon ≈ 3 units, Tue ≈ 7, Wed ≈ 5, Thu ≈ 9, Fri ≈ 4 (relative scale).
Each bar displays a numeric value label (e.g., “3”, “7”, etc.) that is visible when the bar reaches its final height.
At time 0 s all bars have zero height (no visible bar).
The bars grow from zero to their final heights with easing (slow start and slow end) rather than moving at a constant speed.
The tallest bar (Thu) is visually highlighted at the end (e.g., brighter color, outline, or glow) and remains highlighted for at least 0.5 s before the video ends.
No bar, label, or highlight touches or crosses the outer frame edge; there is a clear margin around all elements.
The bars are evenly spaced horizontally and aligned on a common baseline, forming a clean grid layout.
Something meaningful (bar growth, label appearance, or highlight change) occurs in every second of the 6‑second clip (no dead‑air intervals).
The first bar begins to grow within the first 0.5 s of the video (no empty opening).
The final frame holds still (no further animation) for at least 0.5 s before the video ends.
The color palette used for bars, labels, and the highlight is harmonious and the highlight contrasts appropriately with its bar color.
The video is free of visual glitches, flicker, overlapping text, or rendering artifacts.
